instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the night before: soak the dried shiitake in 1/4 cup hot water. Keep them in the fridge if it's overnight.
Squeeze the mushrooms dry, trim off the tough stems, and chop them fine. That should be about 2 tbsp.

Peel and devein the shrimp. Toss them in a bowl with 1/2 tsp of the sugar, the pinch of baking soda and 1 tbsp water. Leave them 15 minutes, then rinse them under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well and chop them roughly.

While the shrimp sit, put the pork in a large bowl with the remaining 1 1/2 tsp sugar, the cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, salt and white pepper. Stir in one direction with chopsticks or a wooden spoon for about 5 to 8 minutes, until it turns into a sticky paste that clings to the bowl.
Add the shrimp and keep stirring in the same direction for about 3 minutes. Stir in the mushrooms, vegetable oil, oyster sauce and sesame oil for another minute or two.

Peel the carrot and mince 1 tbsp of it very fine. Put 2 tbsp of filling in the center of a wrapper. Gather the sides up around it to make an open cup, pack the filling in, and press the top flat. Repeat with the rest, then top each with a pinch of carrot.
Line a steamer with parchment and set the first 6 siu mai in it, about 1 inch apart. Pour water into a wok or pot so it sits 1/2 inch below the steamer's bottom, and bring it to a simmer.

Steam over medium heat for 9 minutes. You're cooking the filling to 165°F, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open. It's done when the pork has no pink and the shrimp are opaque.
Steam the second batch the same way, topping up the water with boiling water if it runs low. Serve with the chili garlic sauce on the side.
advance_prep_notes: soak the dried shiitake at least 2 hours ahead, or overnight
method_notes: The lead is The Woks of Life (5 from 23): ground pork, shrimp treated with sugar and baking soda, shiitake, oyster sauce, steamed 9 minutes per batch. Written at half the lead's amounts, so 12 dumplings. A second page (Takes Two Eggs, 5 from 1) agrees on the filling and steams for 7 to 8 minutes with a 165°F target. The lead's 2 hour mushroom soak is the only ahead step; the wrappers can be thin Hong Kong style rounds or square wonton wrappers.
